editorText:
Although Johns flag ship, the Icarus, didn’t bolster the flashy facilities other specialist teams demanded on their ships, Walker's was the tightest corvette in the fleet. It had one thing that other ships couldn't distill through programming or hardened conformity—trust. It’s equipment was old, John insisted it was more dependable than the newer systems which  hadn’t been battle proven. He knew the ship and he felt it knew him.

John pressed his trigger finger along the cold steel frame of the final truss before the Iris’s ramp door. He waited patiently as the pilot called down the final closing distances. He checked his rifle restraints, tight and firm, any unaccounted drag could spell disaster.

The protectant rifle had been issued in its Sherpa configuration, featured a modern lattice (Add emphasis that FEA annalysis was used in generating the rifles interchangeable stock) stock connected to a thermal core integrated with the primary firing mechanism. The Sherpa build effectively mitigated issues related to condensation buildup and potential jams, particularly in extremely cold weather conditions.

“5 seconds out… mark.. ” John and his team held a couple seconds more, allowing a distance between the landing point they could close in on.

John could feel the cold piercing through his leather gloves as he took a deep breath of regulated air. At an altitude of 30,000 ft, the air was too thin to breathe, let alone fully focus on the complex terrain to navigate below. Nothing but the loud hum of the Icarus engines could be heard. The steel belly of her internal shell was intermittently excited by the lick of the amber Jump light illuminating the stern faces of John's men behind fogged helmet visors. John reassuringly placed his right arm on Lieutenant Vang’s shoulder firmly as the intercom's static engaged over the launch bay megaphone.

“Goooood Morning Ladies, Gentleman, and you re-sleeved motherless bastards” Tex sighed, he hated the mockery having already passed over once before. “Sorry to jump the frostbite on you this morning... This is on a need-to-know basis, level 6 clearance only. Command picked up a distress signal from a beacon, which appeared to be an old United Nations outpost from the  back in 2023. What’s strange though is that all 3 Lidar Thermal magnetic scans of the area detected nothing on the ground. After adjusting for fog, we were able to pick up a structure between the mountains. It is expected that on approach, you will encounter extreme sound on your scanners due to metal deposits in the mountains, along with the fog scattering radar. Once boots are on the ground, apply transfer functions to your radar so you can scan through the fog. What you need to know is that this facility could be the main research facility for the first AI prototypes of the new army. Your mission is to locate the facility and extract any information you can. AI are to be shot on-site and recovered for extraction. Remember, those bastards offed their own creator! Proceed with caution. Over and out!”.

As soon as the jump light turned green, the jump door at the rear of the plane began to lower. Cold air filled the hangar bay, John and his team at the ready. In timed sequence one by one they exited the aircraft falling into a seamless string of souls plummeting toward the earth.

John felt the pressure of 200 km an hour winds compress against his suit as he neared terminal velocity. His smile surged with adrenaline while he gleaned through the thick mist below. What remained of the limited visibility made keeping eye contact with the others difficult. He flicked a reassuring thumbs-up to his squad descending behind him, then gave the signal to close formation on him. The others leaned in streamlining themselves to catch up, leveling off with him in a tight V-Formation. They glided with precision in unison, condensation drops flicking across their visors in rapid succession.

John pinched his wedding finger against his palm, engaging his comms designed for high-altitude high-velocity transmission, “Alright Team, let's keep our sectors tight, your suits and gear in COG mode right until we clear the mountain top. Tau will run you through it all the same. We’ve done this in our sleep plenty of times.”

Tau’s visor lit up with a detailed Three Dimensional map of the mountain tops terrain, a fourth dimension of information detailed altitudes against visibility and turbulence charts while their locations closed across the map on the distress beacon pinging away persistently.

A sudden rush of turbulence scattered their formation slightly, Tex breaking off for a brief second, Shai disappeared from his right peripheral. Unphased they reformed in shared silence. Their HUDS spatial metrics made keeping form like steering a space ship inside the lane of an arcade machine, except the coin slot on this machine was jammed. No resets.

“We’re approaching the Crest, twenty five thousand feet, I’m picking up Echo visuals now”, said Tau. Their HUDS drew on from the radar visuals of the mountain tops drawing a series of winding valleys and passes below “Slowing Descent” Said Tau. One false move could spell death in seconds, yet she spoke calmly. “Vis will be hit and miss  between twenty and eighteen thousand, from fourteen thousand feet, we’ll need to rely on IR trails to as a failsafe, weather is too thick there for radar”.  “Check your trail ejection gates haven’t frozen over, we don’t want to be tailing you blind” Said John. Tau pivoted, speeding ahead of the others, breaking off from the V formation. She pinched her palm four times in rapid succession, immediately two small ports about a foot apart on her lower back propped out momentarily in timed successions,  Small specks of condensation trails fanned out behind her in parrallel.

“actuation contrails confirmed Tau, we’ll track your tail through the clouds once we hit them so we don’t lose visual… or rear end you” Said John. “Try to keep up…” Tau joked light heartedly.

Tau anticipated that any number of simulated exercises couldn’t prepare the best of teams whole heartedly for the unpredictable weather of the Himalayas. Yet in that moment the small team enjoyed the serenity of the dive, reforming beside each other, rapidly approaching the uncertainty of the fog below, they passed glances back and forth. It wasn’t often they got to deploy so remotely. And while all the training they had undergone leading up to this moment had been performed with distinction, it felt exactly as that, a performance. In that dive, they were away from the orchestrations , the ever watching eyes. They felt themselves for the first time since they could remember. The cold unpredictable winds would soon engulf them, they embraced the inchoate. Untrammeled they flew like elementals.

“Remember guys” said Shai, “Don’t hold your breath…”. The crest of the mountains rapidly approached, the snow caps slowly rose up to meet the sun, consuming it’s warm alpenglow faster than it could set. Then the sky became entirely devoid of color, turning to none other than a blur of fleeting wind, and wet snow.

The four Protectant soldiers were swallowed up by a cloud, disappearing from each others vision intermittently. The deeper they entered the womb the more they felt like they were flying through a lake in the sky. Pressing currents fought against their bodies as the mountain updraft battled their descent. “I’m picking something up on my short range radar”. Tau veered her heading slightly avoiding something by a few feet.

Suddenly what felt like a cliff wall smashed against Tex’s side as he trailed, erupting into a screeching ball of dark mist engulfing Shai behind him. Shai’s visor completely blacked out in a dark red and brown hue,  blood and guts strewn across her visor. “Tex!” She screamed. Tex groaned and coughed in agony, as he barrel rolled erratically away from the group. Tau and John maintained their trajectory calmly while Shai watched her friend drift off  her radar. She fought to maintain direction with the Tau and John, while she wiped away the red goop from her helmet visor.  Tex let out a panicked grunt. He mustered all the strength that remained, forcing out an arm from his side he countered the spin just enough to regain control. “Fuck.. I’ve lost radar.. Visor’s all pranged up”. Adrenaline coursed through his veins as he re-calibrated, searching for the others. For a moment he saw his team mates contrails than they were gone as soon as they’d appear. His imagination played tricks on him. “Guys!! I can’t keep a steady fix on you, I’m flying blind!”.

“I got you” Tau tapped her index fingers on both hands in 3 successions simultaneously. The trail ports on her lower back she’d tested earlier, opened up. A second later a smooth laminar trail of thermal smoke spewed out behind her. The smoke lit up Tex’s HUD like a glowing amber road of dust. They weren't far off, but in the opposite direction to his bearing. “So I was imagining” He thought to himself. “I’ve got your trail” said Tex, “coming around now”.

“What the fuck was that” Said Shai.  The last remaining specks of blood clinging to her visor washed away by the barrage of wet wind. “A hawk?”. “Too dam big for a hawk” Tex replied. “Hawks can’t survive above twenty thousand feet, lungs are too small, likely a Himalayan griffin vulture” Said Tau. “Must have been riding the updraft to higher vantage points.” Said John. “Whatever it was” Tex grunted “big bastard hit harder than servo butter chicken at 2am in the morning” Tex concluded. “Well thanks to that big chicken, if we keep this up we’re going to burn through our thermal smoke before we even pass through the densest pocket, then we’re all up shits creek”. “My suits pretty banged up, my profiles off, and I can’t make out a darn thing from the HUD because it’s smashed to shit.” Frustration seeped through Tex’s words.

“Any suggestions other than bird facts”. Said Tex. “ I’m coming to you Tex, follow my guidance while I bring you in line” John was calm in his directive. “Copy that cap” Tex responded.

“Trail cold” Said Tau “we’re at reserve limit”. The thermal amber twin trail vanished into a mist from Tex’s HUD, now devoid of color. He was flying blind again. “Pitch gently right” John’s voice was easy and steady “Pitching…” Tex edged his arm out a little rotating his body slowly. Now without any reference to orient from he relied solely on John’s guidance. “Pitch good!, yaw right 3 degrees.. I almost have you…easy…easy… hold… pitch back a little, got ya!!”  Tex, felt his suit link to Johns. “We’re going to have to tandem until we break the crest cloud.. Tau, I need you to ease up girl so we can  match pace”, “Kitten, adjust suit drag to match John’s speed” said Tau, “Right there with you” Chimed kitten.

Control surfaces scattered across Tau’s suit edged out gently, slowing her descent just enough to match John and Tex. “Vitals steadying” said Shai. “Always steady, wasn’t scared for a moment, don’t know what you’re talking about” Tex joked, “just the thought of the impending bromance got the blood pumping a little’s all”.  An awkward silence fell upon them all, then a moment later, color filled Tex’s visor once more, painting slopes of rock and snow, he let out a sigh of relief as they left the cloud.

“Sorry big guy, but I think we should break up” said John as he decoupled from Tex, “It’s ok” Tex responded, drifting back into line speeding up ahead of John. “I’m more into holding hands and long beach walks..” Joked Tex, Shai chuckled “It’s not just you big guy, Navy relationships are often fleeting…”, “Pffft baha” Tau spat it, crippled by the dry engineers weakness for puns.

“Aaah guys! are you getting these strange fixed static lines on your radar?” Shai was hesitant, having little background knowledge of her suit’s inbuilt systems. After all, her technical aptitude was in medicine and linguistics, not Engineering. “No! that’s real!!” shot Tao.

____Needs work joining these two sections. They just cleared the worst section. Haven’t entered the black out section. Bridge onto the chute deploy.

“Commander, I am picking up strange density readings coming from the face of the mountain approaching fast at approximately 1000 feet. Recommend chute deploy at 1500, sir.” John locked his sight on the fast-approaching density signature. “Alright men on me. Deploy in 3, 2, 1,” several parachutes shot out from the men’s packs in almost precision unison. “Deploy your Ram Heads on my mark, men!” John aimed his Sherpa rifle down below his feet about 30 meters above the signature, allowing a safe descent for his men to inspect the anomaly. As he sighted the cliff face. Geometric software built into the helmet and suit sensors analyzed the cliff face for the safest insertion points displaying them eloquently across John and his team mates HUDS, a row of orange led points lit up in their Helmets inner shell, creating an alert atmosphere which sent blood veining through their bodies. Each of John's teams shouldered their rifles with agility and finesse, firing their grapples directly at their grapple points, Tex prematurely firing his to the others for that slightly compensated loading time, afterall he weighed 120kg. In almost unison, the team retracted inward to the face eased in by the drag of their shoots.

John and his men ever so carefully minded each step, delicately repelling down the face to an exposed landing concealed within the icy crest of the mountain. Recessed into the mountain face, a small landing presented a cavernous entrance inside the mountain's belly.

As they neared the edge of the cavern lip, their shoot strings detached as their suit’s rear thrusters activated burning an array of hot blue pulsed hydrogen explosions. In a pendulum motion, boots flew through the cold air, crashing firmly into the icy cliff's face as their knees bent in to absorb the blow, sending snow and rock silently falling to the depths below. Of course, John and his team did this with extreme confidence, coupled with the suit’s inbuilt ability to absorb shock and implement athlete like prowess in their every movement.

“Retrieve shoots,” John was calculated in his timing. The others engaged a spinning mechanism on their packs which wound up their main shoots like a tight-knit spider thread retracting back into the rear of the suit. Kinetically charged wires that splayed out like a thread of hardened bones when activated would cage the chute out again in the event they needed to redeploy the chute cache.  “Repel on me, not a sound,” John quietly ushered to his men. the chute could also act as a solar array if the occupant becomes stranded in space, to recharge power cells and keep the suit flying solo in the event they become abandoned.

“I see nothing, Commander, but my sensors are picking up faint signals dead ahead. I’m going to take a closer look.” Approaching the end of the cave to what seemed to be nothing but iced over rock, John engaged reverse thermal mode on his Sherpa rifle. The rifle let out a mechanical click then hissed as it inverted its cooling cycle, a small blue flame emitting from an outlet on the rifle's end. Slowly a small section of ice melted away to reveal a cold steel surface. “I’ve located what appears to be the entrance to the facility.” John gripped a cylindrical red device on his utility belt aggressively yanking it from it’s fastener. As he did this a small green light activated on the top of the device now firmly in his hand. “Deploying a thermite grenade! stand back!.” He pressed the green light which now turned red, accompanied by an electronic charging sound, and hurled the cylinder in an underarm rolling motion as both ends of the cylinder pointed to the side walls of the cave, the grenade came to a stop at it’s belly. Suddenly, from both ends of the cylindric device a vibrant burst of energy shot out, spitting a hot molten slither to each siding wall of the cavern, a swirling mixture of molten metal and intense heat shot vertically from the slither to the roof of the cave creating a visually captivating display of vibrant colors as it burnt.. The core of the thermite grenade housed a composite material consisting of nano-engineered thermite particles compacted tightly into individually charged cylinders. The heat generated was not only intense but also selectively directed to maximize its impact on the targeted surface.. Gradually, the icy wall receded, revealing behind it old blast doors seeming unscathed, preserved by the ice. “Commander, we are clear for entry, ready on your command.” “Proceed with caution, Captain.”

“Techy, you’re up,” John called, his voice cutting through the tense silence.

Tao stepped forward, the dim glow of her helmet's visor catching the light as she approached the door's terminal. With a practiced motion, she pressed a small, recessed button on the side of her helmet. A sleek, cable-like appendage unfurled from a hidden port near her wrist, writhing slightly as though alive. The moment she brought it close to the terminal’s data port, the device seemed to awaken.

Tiny tendrils extended from the cable’s tip, swaying gently in the air like they were searching for something unseen. One by one, the tendrils latched onto the port’s internal connections, snapping into place with a faint, metallic whisper. The rest of the cable retracted smoothly into its housing, leaving the connection secure.

“Establishing communication protocol,” Tao said evenly, her voice calm as her HUD began to light up with streams of incoming data.

The terminal screen flickered to life, mirroring the information spilling across her visor. A cascade of raw data scrolled too quickly for the untrained eye, but Tao’s focused gaze parsed it with precision. She worked seamlessly, fingers hovering near the terminal controls while her HUD fed her the details.

“I’m in,” she murmured, a hint of satisfaction threading through her voice as a structured menu unfolded:

System Date: Dec 21, 2174

UNC Facility Details

Capacity: 2000

Occupancy: 2%

Active Occupants: 0

Commission Status: Inactive, awaiting decommission

Purpose: Weapons Research Facility

Commanding Officer: Cmdr. Taggard

Last Active Status: Dec 21, 2024

Tao’s eyes darted across the list, taking in the stark emptiness of the facility’s current state. “Looks like this place has been a ghost town for a while... but the systems are still waiting for something—or someone,” she muttered, her hand hovering over the next command as the silence around her deepened.

Running a full system reboot, bubbles stepped back from the terminal Rifle trained on the door seem. A hiss of steam bellowed gently down the doors seem as they relentlessly screeched grinding steel and rubble. Icicles crashed from the caves canopy to the ground. John held his breath, the steam cleared way before a long winding dark tunnel presenting several locked shut doors beckoned by a series of numbers and titles dimming softly against the lingering empty dark. “Commander we have access, it appears to be the facility, no traces of life, Hud shows to have 0 active occupants, what are your orders?”. Met by silence John and his men looked back and forth between one another, to be interrupted by a sudden firm command. “the previous occupants have been deemed hostile. Permission to use lethal force on site, salvage any data possible and await further instruction”. “Roger that”. Unsurprised and relatively at ease john nods his head and his man walk through the hallways as though taking a stroll in the park. Rifles at ease, bubbles lets out an aww of surprise, “It’s as though the facility was active yesterday, everything still seems operational, I’m getting several system interface responses and network activity. It’s almost as if the facility is still in operation, still linked…” John and his men continue to walk through the halls. “We are looking for the server rooms, keep your eyes peeled for Room DS1343”.

The halls wound on endlessly filling the men with a sense of insecurity in that they may not find their way back, or to return under attack would almost entail a long drawn out engagement, should they be fronted by an ambush scenario. Although silent the facility still felt alive, clean, maintained. Cabling clad along the walls red blue green orange, like veins spoke of the complexity and interconnectivity of the infrastructure which ran deep within the mountain, this was no ordinary research facility. There was a strange presence that the facility itself was aware of their presence as the halls lit up only to revert back to gloomy darkness as the men passed through, waiting dormant for the right opportunity. The deeper in the thicker the cable bundling became.

“DS1343 I have it here Sir”, Announced Lieutenant Vang. “Nice one Tech! hold your position until we arrive, I’ve been informed that you will be retrieving the data alone on this one, need to know only basis”.

“But sir what of the bypass procedures”->

“Commander has given the procedure in a command executable. I won’t be needed.”

“Roger sir standing by for your perimeter check”.

 John approaching Wolfgang hugging the cave face he had used to advance to the door, pressed up against the wall rifle ready. Trained on the server hold room doors ready to breach. Wolfgang plugged his Hud in clearing the doors followed by Johns rifle tip scanning the server rows. John had exited as soon as he had entered. “Clear!”. At this Vang headed into the room and plugged directly into the main HMI to begin the data extraction process. “This may take some time John, I’ll be fine, don’t stray too far”. “Copy that Wolfgang”.

John departs from his team captured by an insignia, he orders his team to continue the search without him, the room has been scanned although he feels drawn to this room and orders them to move on to cover more ground. Describe the halls.

Deploy in 3, 2, 1,” several parachutes shot out from the men’s packs in almost precision unison. “Deploy your Ram Heads on my mark, men!” John aimed his Sherpa rifle down below his feet about 30 meters above the signature, allowing a safe descent for his men to inspect the anomaly. As he sighted the cliff face. Geometric software built into the helmet and suit sensors analyzed the cliff face for the safest insertion points displaying them eloquently across John and his team mates HUDS, a row of orange led points lit up in their Helmets inner shell, creating an alert atmosphere which sent blood veining through their bodies. Each of John's teams shouldered their rifles with agility and finesse, firing their grapples directly at their grapple points, Tex prematurely firing his to the others for that slightly compensated loading time, afterall he weighed 120kg. In almost unison, the team retracted inward to the face eased in by the drag of their shoots.

John and his men ever so carefully minded each step, delicately repelling down the face to an exposed landing concealed within the icy crest of the mountain. Recessed into the mountain face, a small landing presented a cavernous entrance inside the mountain's belly.

As they neared the edge of the cavern lip, their shoot strings detached as their suit’s rear thrusters activated burning an array of hot blue pulsed hydrogen explosions. In a pendulum motion, boots flew through the cold air, crashing firmly into the icy cliff's face as their knees bent in to absorb the blow, sending snow and rock silently falling to the depths below. Of course, John and his team did this with extreme confidence, coupled with the suit’s inbuilt ability to absorb shock and implement athlete like prowess in their every movement.

“Retrieve shoots,” John was calculated in his timing. The others engaged a spinning mechanism on their packs which wound up their main shoots like a tight-knit spider thread retracting back into the rear of the suit. Kinetically charged wires that splayed out like a thread of hardened bones when activated would cage the chute out again in the event they needed to redeploy the chute cache.  “Repel on me, not a sound,” John quietly ushered to his men. the chute could also act as a solar array if the occupant becomes stranded in space, to recharge power cells and keep the suit flying solo in the event they become abandoned.

“I see nothing, Commander, but my sensors are picking up faint signals dead ahead. I’m going to take a closer look.” Approaching the end of the cave to what seemed to be nothing but iced over rock, John engaged reverse thermal mode on his Sherpa rifle. The rifle let out a mechanical click then hissed as it inverted its cooling cycle, a small blue flame emitting from an outlet on the rifle's end. Slowly a small section of ice melted away to reveal a cold steel surface. “I’ve located what appears to be the entrance to the facility.” John gripped a cylindrical red device on his utility belt aggressively yanking it from it’s fastener. As he did this a small green light activated on the top of the device now firmly in his hand. “Deploying a thermite grenade! stand back!.” He pressed the green light which now turned red, accompanied by an electronic charging sound, and hurled the cylinder in an underarm rolling motion as both ends of the cylinder pointed to the side walls of the cave, the grenade came to a stop at it’s belly. Suddenly, from both ends of the cylindric device a vibrant burst of energy shot out, spitting a hot molten slither to each siding wall of the cavern, a swirling mixture of molten metal and intense heat shot vertically from the slither to the roof of the cave creating a visually captivating display of vibrant colors as it burnt.. The core of the thermite grenade housed a composite material consisting of nano-engineered thermite particles compacted tightly into individually charged cylinders. The heat generated was not only intense but also selectively directed to maximize its impact on the targeted surface.. Gradually, the icy wall receded, revealing behind it old blast doors seeming unscathed, preserved by the ice. “Commander, we are clear for entry, ready on your command.” “Proceed with caution, Captain.”
“Techy, you’re up,” John called, his voice cutting through the tense silence.

Tao stepped forward, the dim glow of her helmet's visor catching the light as she approached the door's terminal. With a practiced motion, she pressed a small, recessed button on the side of her helmet. A sleek, cable-like appendage unfurled from a hidden port near her wrist, writhing slightly as though alive. The moment she brought it close to the terminal’s data port, the device seemed to awaken.

Tiny tendrils extended from the cable’s tip, swaying gently in the air like they were searching for something unseen. One by one, the tendrils latched onto the port’s internal connections, snapping into place with a faint, metallic whisper. The rest of the cable retracted smoothly into its housing, leaving the connection secure.
“Establishing communication protocol,” Tao said evenly, her voice calm as her HUD began to light up with streams of incoming data.

The terminal screen flickered to life, mirroring the information spilling across her visor. A cascade of raw data scrolled too quickly for the untrained eye, but Tao’s focused gaze parsed it with precision. She worked seamlessly, fingers hovering near the terminal controls while her HUD fed her the details.
“I’m in,” she murmured, a hint of satisfaction threading through her voice as a structured menu unfolded:
System Date: Dec 21, 2174
UNC Facility Details
Capacity: 2000
Occupancy: 2%
Active Occupants: 0
Commission Status: Inactive, awaiting decommission
Purpose: Weapons Research Facility
Commanding Officer: Cmdr. Taggard
Last Active Status: Dec 21, 2024

Tao’s eyes darted across the list, taking in the stark emptiness of the facility’s current state. “Looks like this place has been a ghost town for a while... but the systems are still waiting for something—or someone,” she muttered, her hand hovering over the next command as the silence around her deepened.

Running a full system reboot, bubbles stepped back from the terminal Rifle trained on the door seem. A hiss of steam bellowed gently down the doors seem as they relentlessly screeched grinding steel and rubble. Icicles crashed from the caves canopy to the ground. John held his breath, the steam cleared way before a long winding dark tunnel presenting several locked shut doors beckoned by a series of numbers and titles dimming softly against the lingering empty dark. “Commander we have access, it appears to be the facility, no traces of life, Hud shows to have 0 active occupants, what are your orders?”. Met by silence John and his men looked back and forth between one another, to be interrupted by a sudden firm command. “the previous occupants have been deemed hostile. Permission to use lethal force on site, salvage any data possible and await further instruction”. “Roger that”. Unsurprised and relatively at ease john nods his head and his man walk through the hallways as though taking a stroll in the park. It’s almost as if the facility is still in operation, still linked…” John and his men continue to walk through the halls. “We are looking for the server rooms, keep your eyes peeled for Room DS1343”.

The halls wound on endlessly filling the men with a sense of insecurity in that they may not find their way back, or to return under attack would almost entail a long drawn out engagement, should they be fronted by an ambush scenario. Although silent the facility still felt alive, clean, maintained. Cabling clad along the walls red blue green orange, like veins spoke of the complexity and interconnectivity of the infrastructure which ran deep within the mountain, this was no ordinary research facility. There was a strange presence that the facility itself was aware of their presence as the halls lit up only to revert back to gloomy darkness as the men passed through, waiting dormant for the right opportunity. The deeper in the thicker the cable bundling became.

“Commander has given the procedure in a command executable. I won’t be needed.”

John approaching Wolfgang hugging the cave face he had used to advance to the door, pressed up against the wall rifle ready. Trained on the server hold room doors ready to breach.
